entries.note: The central assessment is a subjective judgment of invasiveness and annoyance. The explanation of Apple's desperation also attributes a motive.
The normalization turns a qualified impression into a categorical assertion that LLMs lack utility. The source chiefly expresses a judgment of their worth.

entries.test: Public task evaluations and demonstrated uses would establish whether any LLM performed even one task well by publication.
entries.note: The 'iPhone moment' comparison is imprecise, but the categorical denial of any task performed well has a testable plain reading.

entries.test: Public reliability evaluations, contemporary coverage, and statements by prominent AI supporters would establish the reported inconsistency and warnings against trusting outputs.
entries.note: Reporting that supporters warn against trusting output is not identical to asserting categorically that output cannot be trusted.

entries.test: Public demonstrations and independent evaluations available by publication would show whether LLM systems completed tasks autonomously with consistent, reliable, reproducible results.
entries.note: The source hedges the impression of being antithetical to autonomy, but directly asserts the capability limitations retained here.

entries.test: Contemporary ChatGPT documentation and independent instruction-following evaluations would establish whether its capabilities were clear and its execution dependable.
entries.note: The 'different product' conclusion is rhetorical, but the present capability and reliability assertions are testable.

entries.test: Company financial disclosures and infrastructure announcements would establish the scale of generative AI investment, while revenues, returns, and valuations would test the bubble characterization.
entries.note: The preceding sentence supplies both 'hundreds of billions' and the bubble characterization, although the selected excerpt omits them.
The source attributes an exclusive underlying purpose to the companies' shared ideal; the normalization drops 'entirely.' Public capability evidence cannot settle that exclusive private motive.

entries.test: Public deployments and evaluations available by publication would establish whether generative AI had successfully replaced human work in the manner described.
entries.note: In context, 'it' refers to the promised automation of humans out of the picture. The normalization broadens this to generative AI working in any sense.

entries.test: Public investment returns, consumer adoption, and SaaS and enterprise IT growth through June 9, 2026 would test whether justifying the investment required the specified consumer and enterprise breakthrough by that date.
entries.note: This asserts a necessary condition for investment payoff, rather than predicting that the breakthrough will occur. Its twelve-month deadline has passed.

entries.test: Public studies tracing low-quality online content to OpenAI and Microsoft tools and measuring its effect on information quality would test the claimed causal relationship.
entries.note: The insult does not erase the substantive assertion that their LLM deployments degraded online information.
The source offers an impression that Altman stumbled into ChatGPT and was surprised by its reception. The normalization shifts this to accidentally achieving its success and omits the surprise.

entries.test: Public adoption, customer research, and purchasing evidence would show whether LLM text and image generation met substantial demand beyond reducing the cost of existing work.
entries.note: The following clause supplies the cost-cutting context. The claim has a plain reading about demand and uses, despite its dismissive wording.

The normalization makes 'three years later' explicitly mean three years after ChatGPT and omits the source's production-plus-quality-control standard. Task performance is testable, but the industry's asserted lack of genuine interest concerns private motivation.
